0.long_answer: Cor triatriatum dexter is a rare congenital heart defect that results from the complete persistence of the right sinus venosus valve during embryonic development. In a normal heart, the right sinus valve regresses as the atria are remodeled; however, in this condition, its persistence leads to the formation of a membrane that subdivides the right atrium into two distinct chambers. This abnormal membrane is located in the same atrium as the coronary sinus valve, potentially interfering with normal blood flow. The defect may be associated with symptoms such as cyanosis and could require surgical intervention if it leads to significant hemodynamic compromise. It is important to distinguish this condition from other types of cor triatriatum, such as cor triatriatum sinistrum, which affects the left atrium.
